To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the rhizosphere of plants with high nitrogen (N) requirements is characterized by a lower pH than the bulk soil, (ii) this rhizosphere pH is a function of the N requirement of the plant, (iii) this lower rhizosphere pH results in an increased availability of N to plants, and (iv) the rhizospheric pH effect on N availability to plants can be considered as a priming effect.

1) The RPE is a complex process involving multiple factors and interactions, 2) The RPE can be positive, neutral, or negative depending on the plant species, soil properties, and environmental factors, and 3) The RPE has significant implications for soil fertility and crop productivity.

the rhizosphere is a complex environment, which is influenced by the plant, the microbe and the soil.
soil pH is an important factor that influences soil microbial activity, nutrient availability and plant growth, but the mechanisms by which it does so are not well understood.
